text:
Samira N: hey folks, quick onboarding hiccup. my docker-compose postgres keeps crashing with "FATAL: data directory has wrong ownership" after i mounted ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
Leo M: welcome! that usually means the host folder is owned by root or your UID doesn't match the postgres user in the container (often 999). what OS are you on?
Samira N: macOS (m1). i cloned repo and created pgdata with mkdir and chown myuser.
Nina H: on mac with Docker Desktop the container user ids don't map the same; easiest is to let the image initialize the volume: remove the host mount, bring the container up, let it create files, then copy out sample files if needed.
Samira N: hmm i need persistent data between restarts. any safe approach?
Leo M: create pgdata but chown to 999:999 (postgres uid/gid). `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` usually fixes it. or use a named volume in compose so docker manages ownership: `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and top-level `volumes: { pgdata: {} }`.
Samira N: tried chown 999:999 and it started. thanks. another thing: my host tools expect Postgres on 5432 but i changed compose to map 5434:5432 to avoid conflict. how should i configure tests on host vs containers?
Nina H: containers talk to service name `postgres:5432`. Host tools should use localhost:5434. Add a note in README and .env.local: `DB_HOST=postgres` for container runs and `HOST_DB_PORT=5434` for host tests.
Samira N: saved that. QA Bot: reminder: do not commit passwords. add .env.local to .gitignore.
Samira N: will do. thanks y'all!
